_: The texts the legal review relies on. tools/statutes.js fetches each one once a week, from the e-Gov law API, from GitHub's site-policy repository and from the sites of the services named under pages, and compares it with the value recorded here. A change is proposed as a pull request; a value is recorded only when the operator, having read the difference, adds the label `record` (tools/record.js).

text.missing: the article or item was not found
text.title: law title
text.issueTitle: Weekly check: a statute or a term that the legal review relies on may have changed
text.issueHead: The weekly check on {when} found these different from the recorded values.
text.issueFoot: Read the changed text, check docs/legal-review.md and the policies, then record the new value in verification/statutes.json.
text.closed: The check on {when} found everything as recorded. Closing.
text.prTitle: Record the changed texts the legal review relies on
text.seedTitle: Record the texts the legal review relies on
text.prHead: The watch found these different from the recorded values. Each change is shown below; a statute is shown as a difference of its sentences.
text.noOld: No earlier text is recorded, so the whole text is shown.
text.seeded: {n} texts that match their recorded values are stored for the first time, so that a later change can be shown as a difference.
text.prFoot: Read each change, then check docs/legal-review.md and the policies. To record it, add the label `record`: a workflow merges this into main, runs the checks on the result first, and merges only if they pass. The merge button would leave the merge without the disclosure line that the checks across the repositories count, so it is not used. If a policy must change too, change it first in a pull request of its own.
text.openPr: This repository does not let workflows open pull requests, so the proposal is here. The branch `statutes/record` holds it: open the pull request with this link, then add the label `record` to it. {link}

changelog.line: - The weekly watch found that a text the legal review relies on changed. The operator read the difference, and the new values and texts are recorded in `verification/statutes.json` and `verification/statutes-texts.json` (#PR).
changelog.seedLine: - The weekly watch stored the texts it compares, without changing any recorded value, so that a later change can be shown as a difference (#PR).
